notes: ITC-99 official benchmarks from Politecnico di Torino CAD Group (I99T repo).
Formats: bench / blif / edf / vhd. No native Verilog.
All 21 available circuits (b01-b15, b17-b22) acquired as gate-level BLIF (6.5 MB).
BLIF .latch rows lack explicit clock control (I99T README: single-phase global clock GCLK implicit). Yosys reads them as transparent level-latches and optimizes them away.

Clock handling: need to inject GCLK as edge-triggered clock (or convert $dlatch->$dff) for timing ECO experiments. Deferred; ISCAS89 (8 gate-level circuits with real CK) already sufficient for method validation.

The tree moved to data/raw/benchmarks/raw/itc99 after the acquisition; `source_root` is kept as the acquisition-time location and `local_root` gives the current one.  Verify with scratch/verify_benchmark_integrity.py.

b18/b19 are special: the acquisition path now holds a PROJECT-DERIVED re-export (a clock-injected full expansion produced by the 2026-08-04 b18/b19 repair), not the upstream file.  The upstream pin above is VALID (verified byte for byte against the upstream content at the pinned commit); the pristine upstream copies are preserved at experiments/20260804_itc99_probe/bNN_truncated.blif -- the name "truncated" is the project's own misnomer, those files ARE the upstream originals (b18 141,045 B, b19 322,813 B).  `local_sha256` below is the digest of the derived file that sits at the acquisition path today.

label_family_circuits.why_the_13: The physical-label family needs a FROZEN FLOORPLAN whose geometry is transferred from the noise-floor family, so a circuit qualifies only if it has BOTH a ledger in the main family AND a baseline run in the noise-floor family.  Those 7 (base family) qualified.  The extension family adds the 6 that the base family explicitly does not cover and that are physically reachable.  The selection reads the LEDGER ONLY -- no physical outcome can leak into it (see itc99_ext_manifest.json: pool_rule / selection_reads).

derivation_recipe.step_0_upstream: the upstream I99T file at the pinned commit (bench / blif / edf / vhd)
derivation_recipe.step_1_project_tool: the project expands the upstream netlist into data/raw/benchmarks/raw/itc99/{v/bNN.v, bench/bNN.bench, bNN.blif} and injects the implicit single-phase global clock as an edge-triggered clock (the upstream .latch rows carry no explicit clock, so Yosys would optimise the latches away -- see the manifest notes)
derivation_recipe.step_2_synthesis: experiments/20260804_itc99_b18b19_wsl/map_bNN.ys: read_verilog benchmarks/raw/itc99/v/bNN.v -> synth -top bNN -> dfflibmap -liberty <sky130hd .lib> -> abc -liberty <sky130hd .lib> -> clean -> write_verilog -noattr bNN_mapped.v
derivation_recipe.why_it_matters: b18/b19 appear in the paper only as separately reported large examples; they are NOT part of the r30 physical-label family (which uses b01--b13), so this derivation does not touch any published physical number
